log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Support selection and procurement of the components needed for a prototype controller board.","tasks":["Find a component by part number or description and read across its row.","Compare quantities, unit prices, and suppliers for purchasing.","Read component descriptions sequentially to check specifications."],"relations":["Each row links one part number and description to its required quantity, unit price, and supplier.","Technical values and units within a description jointly specify the component."],"roles":["The header names five fields; each subsequent row describes one component.","Part number identifies the item, description distinguishes its specifications, and quantity, unit price, and supplier support purchasing."],"keep_whole":["Part numbers and supplier names are important lookup strings.","Quantities, prices, and technical values with their units should stay together where space permits."],"may_wrap":["Descriptions can wrap at natural phrase or word boundaries.","Headers can wrap at word boundaries; on a fitting layout, some identifiers and supplier names must split."],"same_scale":["All part numbers should share a consistent column width, as should all descriptions and each purchasing field.","Quantity needs less space than the identification and description fields."],"h_vs_v":"A viewport-width table avoids horizontal scrolling but forces identifiers and suppliers to split and makes rows tall. Wider tables preserve lookup strings and reduce row height, at the cost of scrolling across each row."},"designs":[{"widths":[86,100,47,62,64],"strategy":"Fit within 359px, giving the two identification fields the largest shares while accepting broken identifiers, suppliers, and some price text."},{"widths":[186,200,47,91,154],"strategy":"Use a compact scrolling table that keeps identifiers, prices, quantities, and suppliers whole while allowing descriptions to wrap."},{"widths":[186,547,47,91,154],"strategy":"Use a wide scrolling reference table that keeps every cell on one line, making each row compact and descriptions continuous."}]}
